pr_title: metric: add debug information to panicking goroutines in Snapshot
pr_body:
Issue #136186 introduced a seemingly impossible situation in which the internal properties of the prometheus histogram implementation mismatched in a way which caused a panic.

The properties specifically, where `h` is a histogram were `h.upperBounds` and `h.counts[0/1].buckets`. These properties are slices, initialized once, whose references are never modified, lengths never changed, and are never appended to. The length of the `counts` property is set by the length of the `upperBounds` property, which should guarantee that they are always the same length, however given the panic in the above ticket, `upperBounds` somehow became longer than `counts[0/1]`.

While this change cannot tell us how the lengths of each array got to a certain way, it will tell us exactly what the lengths are, which would be the next step if it were to recur. The test in this PR is built in with a time bomb so that if it goes a year without being relevant, the test will start failing, encouraging us to move on and focus on other things.

Epic: none
Fixes: #136186

Release note: None

CC'ing via the CODEOWNERS-based sentry heuristic:
* @cockroachdb/obs-prs

<sub>:owl: Hoot! I am a [Blathers](https://github.com/apps/blathers-crl), a bot for [CockroachDB](https://github.com/cockroachdb). My owner is [dev-inf](https://github.com/orgs/cockroachdb/teams/dev-inf).</sub>

Starting to dig into this ticket, the error seems to be that a histogram with zero buckets was used. On trying to read from `coldCounts.bucket[i]`, it failed with the index zero. Source line for the panic below:

https://github.com/prometheus/client_golang/blob/3583c1e1d085b75cab406c78b015562d45552b39/prometheus/histogram.go#L754

This is in the windowed histogram implementation, it's failing on the line where the system is trying to merge the two histograms, specifically, where it's copying its prev value to a temporary variable.

Counts specifically is the 1th `counts` property on a histogram. A histogram supports two counts objects in an array:

```go
type Histogram struct {
    ...
    counts [2]*histogramCounts
    ...
}

type histogramCounts struct {
    ...
    buckets []uint64
    ...
}
```

Given the panic above, it seems as if the `buckets` property is a zero size slice for the coldCounts during the panic.

Things that have been ruled out:

It seems like we call `Write` into the codebase, a locked path simultaneously with `Observe`, a lock free path which modifies properties used in `Write`. Though this does introduce a race condition, there are no code paths which could change a buckets slice from non-zero length to zero-length. The slice is only ever initialized once, synchronously:

https://github.com/prometheus/client_golang/blob/3583c1e1d085b75cab406c78b015562d45552b39/prometheus/histogram.go#L558
The above race condition should perhaps be explored for possible issues in the future.

There's two possibilities:
1. The first is that the histogram was initialized with no buckets (I need to check that the other class functions would work in this case).
2. The second is that something (the runtime or something else) is modifying the length of the slice beyond what would be expected.

I'll further investigate the first, without know much for the second.

Ensuring setting properly:

upperBounds is only set at:
 - 519
 - 528
 - 552

counts elements are only initialized at:
 - 558
 - 561

buckets are also only initialized on the above two lines, and then never modified. the elements in buckets are touched, but the reference to buckets itself is never mutated

The above PR does change the code so that the lengths of the properties are attached to the panicking goroutine, but I'm leaning towards not releasing it and simply closing this ticket as can't reproduce. What we actually want to see is when, if anywhere the lengths of the slices are modified, which we have no means for attaching handlers to, since they're private properties in library code.

From what I understand about this issue, an impossible situation had been reached when the len(couldCounts.buckets) < len(upperBounds). Both the upperBounds and buckets are initialized once, their headers are never touched, they're never appended to, and their references are never changed.

This is an impossible to reproduce bug, and is likely due to some form of memory corruption.
